description: We're a small team of four who like space, games and explaining science in a simple way. For the hackathon we want to build something playable and educational about life on Mars, using real NASA data and sources. We write code and care about security and clean, reliable software. We'd love to add a designer, a writer or a storyteller, or anyone who just enjoys space and wants to try making a game. Beginners are welcome.
summary:
MARS is an interactive educational web game for children aged 7–12. It combines a 15-Sol Mars mission, resource management, mini-games, 53 educational cards, an interactive knowledge base, and a story featuring two young astronauts, Khurshed and Mohinur. 

We bring the NASA Space Apps Challenge Build a Junior Astronaut Mission Trainer to life by letting children experience the challenges of managing a Mars base. Players manage Life, Energy, and Protection, explore four base sectors, face eight types of crises, and make decisions that affect their mission. 

We believe children should not only learn about space exploration but also experience the thinking behind it. Our game introduces them to engineering trade-offs, limited resources, prioritization, and problem-solving — skills essential for future space explorers. 

Through interactive gameplay, educational cards, mini-games, and a story-driven experience, we turn learning about Mars into an adventure. Players do not simply read about a mission — they become responsible for its success.
details:
How Our Project Works

MISSION: MARS is an interactive educational web game for children aged 7–12. Players take part in a simulated Mars mission, managing a research base over 15 Sols (Martian days). They monitor three main resources — Life, Energy, and Protection — and make decisions that affect the mission. Players explore four base sectors, face eight types of crises, complete 16 mini-games, and discover scientific facts through 53 educational cards. The project also includes an interactive knowledge base and a story-driven mini-series featuring two young astronauts, Khurshed and Mohinur.

What Makes Our Project Beneficial

MISSION: MARS combines interactive entertainment with learning about space science. Instead of simply reading information, children apply their knowledge, make decisions, solve challenges, and observe the consequences of their choices. The project brings together a web game, educational cards with QR codes, a knowledge base, and story-driven content on one platform. The cards can also be used independently, for example, in astronomy lessons, making the project suitable for both learning at home and classroom activities. After the initial download, the game can continue working offline.

What We Aim to Achieve

We aim to make astronomy and space exploration more accessible and engaging for young learners. Through MISSION: MARS, we want to spark children’s interest in science, develop their problem-solving and critical-thinking skills, and help them understand the challenges of establishing a human settlement on another planet.

In the future, we plan to expand the project by creating a full 3D version of the game, adding new missions on the Moon and other planets, producing more animated stories, publishing a printed comic series, and developing educational materials for teachers.

What We Used to Develop Our Project

We used HTML, CSS, and JavaScript to create the MISSION: MARS website and game interface. At the initiative of our programmer, we also used Python to write scripts, create auxiliary working files, and download and process data and photographs.

We also used AI tools:
• Claude — helped our programmer write and improve the website’s code, implement functionality, and bring the team’s technical ideas to life.
• Google Gemini — was used to create animations, images, and visual materials.
• ChatGPT — was used to generate several images and assist in finding NASA-related materials and data.

What Makes Our Project Creative

The creativity of MISSION: MARS lies in combining a game, a comic, and short animated videos into one continuous story. We created our own characters — Khurshed and Mohinur — who experience the Mars mission alongside the children. They are accompanied by a special assistant who guides them through the events and challenges. At the beginning and at the very end of the mission, players watch short 30-second video episodes that complement the gameplay and draw them deeper into the story.

Another special feature is the mission’s collectible notebook. By completing tasks and mini-games and exploring educational cards, children earn stickers, rewards, and new collection items. Their goal is to gradually fill the notebook and collect the entire set while learning more about space.

What We Considered During Development

We considered the children’s age, the accessibility of the gameplay, and the accuracy of the scientific information. We paid particular attention to the real engineering constraints of a Mars mission: limited resources, energy, time, and base capabilities. Players must decide which tasks should take priority because it is impossible to do everything at once. In this way, we demonstrate an important principle of engineering: every decision involves trade-offs, limitations, and consequences.
